identity.real_world_identity_notes: MINI prepared for the MINI CHALLENGE championship's JCW class, running a Damico-tuned 2.0-litre turbo to a 255 bhp target through a Quaife sequential gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither, and a clutch is still needed to pull away.

The championship names the gearbox but not its gear count, so the six gears come from the drive. It is a racing Quaife sequential, and the car provides its own blip, so no claim is made about whether a driver blip would otherwise be needed.
This is a different car from the road-going MINI John Cooper Works Challenge, which is sold with a six-speed manual rather than a sequential.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mini-cooper-jcw.20260816t043015744z-26d913b2 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: The championship's own class page establishes the JCW car and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The championship states a Quaife sequential gearbox, and the live drive selected six gears through a sequential stick with automatic cut and blip.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
